title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement a new generation of gender-responsive national employment policies, including for youth

description.narrative: Egypt’s national development strategy (Vision 2030) encompasses a vision and measurable targets for youth employment (including on unemployment, economic participation, entrepreneurship or vocational and technical education). To operationalise these provisions, the Government of Egypt through its Ministry of Social Solidarity has designed and launched in 2020 and 2021 a national programme entitled "Forsa" ("opportunity"), with the medium-term objective of extending active labour market support to social assistance beneficiaries (currently 2.5M households). The programme has been launched in 8 priority governorates of southern Egypt, including with financing from a WB loan (50M USD in 2020). The programme delivers a variety of services to promote both wage and self-employment, with the objective of "graduating" recipients of social assistance out of poverty. The implementation of the programme has involved a restructuring of the Ministry's set-up, by rationalising, articulating and consolidating projects and departments working around socioeconomic development. It also involved systematising and enhancing the way the Ministry of Social Solidarity partners with other public service providers, including the Government's micro and small enterprise development agency (MSMEDA), and the youth centers of the Ministry of Youth and Sports. The ILO has provided strategic advice to the Ministry in designing and then piloting the Forsa programme through two projects funded by Norway. In 2018 and 2019, as previously reported, the ILO had provided technical assistance to the Minister with the design of active labour market and graduation programmes. This was done in coordination with the World Bank as it prepared for a lending operation to finance the programme. The ILO then implemented capacity development and training of trainers activities for NGOs and Ministry staff, who were previously mostly responsible for cash assistance, not with employability services. Through the project the ILO provides continuous strategic advice to the national unit responsible for the Programme at the Ministry.
